understood_action: Back Ashutosh Sharma and Patrick Cummins first if they reach the auction, and treat the rest of the shortlist as options.
confusions: The yellow box 'Historical pressure-performance indicator; persistence not demonstrated. Its ability to predict IPL 2027 is not established (D15)' - I do not know what persistence means or what D15 is. 'Must-Back' sits right next to a paragraph saying the score 'did not beat the plain (naive) ranking' (batters 42.9% v 46.7%, '80% interval -3.8 pts'), so I cannot tell whether to trust the label. Three names for one idea: 'Clutch Score', 'Pressure Index', 'High-pressure'. '99 (80% range 66-100)' - what is an 80% range? Tags like 'ASSUMPTION A6', 'age UNKNOWN', 'ASSUMPTION A2' on every card with no plain explanation. The Before / With Plan A bars (e.g. Death +3.9 to +22.4) look like a projection of what I will get. Tab row is cut off at phone width ('3 Leade').
sounds_like_forecast: Mild: the 'Before / with Plan A picks' bars (death +3.9 to +22.4) read like a result I would get; 'Must-Back' and 'Hidden Gem' sound like guarantees. Page itself says it is not a forecast and 'Plan A narrows it; it does not close it for certain'.

understood_action: Judge players on the high-pressure balls (the top-20% swing balls) rather than on overall numbers.
confusions: The formula box 'Pressure = leverage x (1 + 0.1.chase pressure + 0.1.below par + 0.1.death + ...)' and the word 'leverage' mean nothing to me. 'Ranked against earlier balls: 80+ = High' - against what? The 'RR v CSK' interactive win-probability chart needs a slider and axis reading I would not do in 2 minutes. The 'hottest cell' heat map (innings 1, over x wickets down) is tiny at phone width. In the example balls, a Low-pressure ball ends in 'WICKET (Caught)' and a 3.0 pressure score, which looks like a contradiction to a cricketer. Win prob 53% shown as 'Medium' with 'wide' tag - unclear. Chart caption 'Medium 50-80 / High 80+ with Pressure Index cut-offs' hard to read.

understood_action: Scroll the ranked lists of batters and bowlers to build a long list; do not rely on exact order.
confusions: The page is about 24,600 px tall, roughly 40 phone screens of dense cards, so nobody can absorb it in 2 minutes. At the size I could view it I could not read the row text (LOW CONFIDENCE on details). I could see the same yellow 'Read with care' box and 'Honest read' caveats at the top, and a long run of repeated cards with pill tags (UNKNOWN, ASSUMPTION). Likely misread: treating rank 1 vs rank 2 as a real gap when the ranges overlap; seeing already-retained players at the top and thinking they are targets.
sounds_like_forecast: Unsure (could not read row text); the shared header says ability to predict IPL 2027 is not established.

understood_action: Do not separate Ashutosh Sharma (99) and Patrick Cummins (97) on score; choose on role, price and availability.
confusions: The headline 'too close to call. Their 80% ranges overlap' is clear, but the radar chart axes ('Clutch score', 'Skill', 'Consistency', 'Holds up (gap)', 'WPA per ball', 'High-pressure sample') are jargon; WPA is never explained in cricket terms. 'RAE per 100 (High)' and 'RSE per 100 (High)' are unexplained. I am comparing a batter with a bowler, so most rows show a dash '-' for one of them and the metrics are not like for like. 'Pressure gap (High - Low) +28.7 / +21.0': is higher good? 'Consistency 80 / 73' vs 'Clutch 99 / 97' - which wins? Season chart with 2024-2026 'runs above expected' markers and 'few balls swing wildly' warning is hard to read. 'Rank within role 2 of 47 (98th pct)' mixes rank and percentile.

understood_action: Our weak spot is batting in the middle and death overs under pressure; Plan A (Cummins, Samad, Ashutosh, Rizvi) narrows it, but do not treat it as settled.
confusions: 'RR trails the league under pressure in 2 of 6 areas' and 'Runs above expected per 100 High-pressure balls' - per 100 of which balls, and is negative bad? Switching Before / Plan A / Plan B changes the bars but Batting powerplay drops 56.0 to 44.1 with Plan A and nobody says why. 'Age profile UNKNOWN' and 'Overseas count: inferred 7 of 20' sit beside confident numbers. 'Best XI' lineup card and 'Impact player' look like a recommended team even though it is a sample. '20-over bowling plan' lists balls bowled (e.g. 402 legal balls) rather than a plan. Bowling strength is shown as ahead of league in all phases but the 'spend' advice is only in small text.
sounds_like_forecast: Yes, mildly: 'Plan A narrows it', 'Plan A adds pressure-proven options' and before/after bars read like a projected improvement, although the page says it is not proof.

understood_action: Pursue Ashutosh Sharma and Patrick Cummins if they reach the pool and the price stays at or below the walk-away number; use Value Picks and Hidden Gems as cheaper options.
confusions: Price lines like 'Rs 0.3-3 cr [ASSUMPTION A6]' and 'Walk-away Rs 3 cr' look like real auction guidance, but small print says they are rule-based bands, not market data. 'Hidden Gem' vs 'Value Pick' vs 'Must-Back' - the tier rules are not on the page. Plan B 'if the price runs away... RR loses about 20% of Plan A's pressure value' - what is pressure value? The 'score against price' scatter (value zone) is tiny. 'Who not to chase' lists Hardik Pandya (score 7, range 1.4-47.6) and Sherfane Rutherford (3.7): a selector will think the model is broken or that they are bad players, when the reason is small samples. 'Contrarian picks' (Prasidh Krishna, Shardul Thakur) with low scores is confusing next to 'Back' advice.
sounds_like_forecast: Mild: 'Must-Back', 'Hidden Gem', and 'RR loses about 20% of Plan A's pressure value' sound like predicted outcomes.

understood_action: Not an action page: it says do not treat the Clutch Score as a predictor of IPL 2027; use it as a record of past pressure play.
confusions: The headline is clear, but the 'Backtest, in plain words' box is stats: 'score 42.9% v naive 46.7% v random pick 50.8% (difference -3.8 pts, 80% interval -17.1 to +3.8 spans zero)'. 'Naive', 'random pick', 'hit rate', 'shrinkage', 'pre-registered', 'Brier' and 'Score = 100 x Phi((sum w.z / sd))' are not meant for me. The bar chart shows the pink Clutch bars at or below the grey/blue bars for batters and bowlers, i.e. the score looks worse than a random pick, yet the rest of the product tells me to back these names. 'Weights' table lists planned weights but the real ones differ (not on this page). Raw codes (D15, D30) leak through.
sounds_like_forecast: No - it explicitly says there is no forecast.

sounds_like_forecast: Mild: the 'Switch rule: RR loses about 20% of Plan A's pressure value' and 'Middle batting -9.7 to -1.4 with Plan A' read like projected gains. The honesty line states it is not a forecast.

understood_action: Pursue Ashutosh Sharma and Patrick Cummins first, only if they reach the auction pool, and read the score as a record rather than a promise.

understood_action: Understand how the score is built: six steps, weights fixed before any ranking, so the model is not tuned to flatter a player.

'Planned weight' vs 'Effective' columns: Match impact is 0.25 for batters but 0 for bowlers, and 'effective' weights differ from planned - I do not follow why. 'Not Scorable (147 of 257 players in scope)' - more than half of players are unscored, buried in a footnote. 'Brier', 'shrinkage', 'logistic model' are unexplained.

understood_action: Judge players on the 80+ pressure balls, and be more cautious with first-innings pressure labels than chase labels.

Table columns 'Brier, all / 1st innings / 2nd innings' - the footnote says a coin flip scores 0.25 and lower is better, which I have to work out myself; 'first-innings models barely do' beat a coin flip, so first-innings Pressure labels are unreliable, but the chart does not mark which balls are first innings.
